newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: VAN DORP TO SHED NON-CORE ACTIVITIES.
newsitem.headline: VAN DORP TO SHED NON-CORE ACTIVITIES.

text.p: Van Dorp Groep NV said on Wednesday it had decided to concentrate on its core activities of office equipment trading and producing diaries.
"For the units which no longer fit the core activities, we will look for new owners who can offer sufficient synergy," the company said in a statement.

Van Dorp's other activities mainly include production and distribution of medical disposables. Last year, it had already transferred this division's production facilities from Britain to the Netherlands and ended a joint venture in the U.S.
Van Dorp said in February it would analyse the group because of disappointing results in recent years. In 1996 it lost 3.6 million guilders, compared with a profit of 2.5 million in 1995.
The company said the analysis had shown that all activities had good prospects in principle, but that Van Dorp could not utilize all of them at short notice.

"The markets in which the units are active are moving strongly so that choices have to be made now," it said. Van Dorp had therefore decided to concentrate on powerful and profitable growth of office goods wholesaling and importing and the production of diaries where it already has sound market shares.
"By concentrating entirely on these activities, the Van Dorp group has potential to become a profitable market player in the Benelux, with growth prospects outside of that area," the company said.
Van Dorp added that its aim was to strengthen its two core divisions through organic growth and takeovers, with a return on equity of more than 15 percent.
The structure of the group will be adapted to this strategy and funds will be made available for the necessary investments and possibly for takeovers, it said.
